title: AsyncET: Asynchronous Representation Learning for Knowledge Graph Entity Typing

problem.claim: Knowledge graph entity typing predicts missing entity types in knowledge graphs.

gap.claim: Using a single hasType relation has limited capability for modeling diverse entity-type relationships in the embedding space.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces multiple auxiliary relations to model complex entity-type relationships.
It proposes an efficient and robust algorithm that groups similar entity types and assigns each group a unique auxiliary relation.
It proposes AsyncET, an asynchronous representation learning framework that alternately updates entity and type embeddings for KGET.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that entity embedding quality gradually improves during training by infusing type information.
The authors report that entity types with different granularities and semantics can be properly modeled in the embedding space.
The authors report substantial improvement over embedding-based methods on KGET and advantages over state-of-the-art neural network methods in model size and inference time.

narrative_sequence.summary: KGET predicts missing entity types in knowledge graphs.
A single hasType relation is limited for representing diverse entity-type relationships.
The paper introduces grouped auxiliary relations and an asynchronous framework with alternating entity and type embedding updates.
The framework is reported to improve entity embeddings and model entity types across different granularities and semantics.
Experiments are reported to improve KGET performance and reduce model-size and inference-time costs relative to neural network methods.

source_observation.claim: The framework alternates entity and type embedding updates while infusing type information into entity representations.

interpretation.claim: Alternating update schedules may help when entity and type representations provide mutually useful training signals.

application.claim: Consider alternating representation updates when designing embedding-based entity-typing systems with auxiliary relation information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the KGET task.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, and experimental conditions are not specified.
The compared embedding-based and neural network methods are not identified.
Ablations, implementation details, and computational-resource settings are not provided.
